source: Save character spacing and facing for a group and re-apply it with the group. The first pose in grid display order is the anchor (position and rotation reference). Every other pose stores a local position offset (in the anchor's frame), relative rotation (vs anchor), maker body height, and Studio object scale on that pose path. Set up Chars and pose Male / Female tags if needed. 2. Select exactly as many characters as poses in Studio. 3. Apply the group (Apply to characters…) so poses map in display order (first pose → anchor character). 4. Arrange characters, then Save positions… without applying another pose in between (see button tooltip if disabled). To apply saved positions — same apply path (same pose order and Chars priority). After poses are applied: • Apply relative positions (global; group bar or Options) — each non-anchor character moves to anchor position + anchor rotation × saved offset (orbits with the anchor) and rotates to anchor rotation × saved relative rotation. source:
Bones adjusted with yellow ABMX sliders in maker tabs are automatically added to this window.

Hover over bones in the list below to see notes (only some bones have them). Bones commented with "ANIMCOR" are used by animation correction system, adjusting them can cause weird effects during gameplay.
BL = Bone length. It's the distance between given bone and its parent. In some cases (like cf_j_spine02/03) effect is pretty obvious, in some not so much. Offset and rotation controls can be used instead, but the effect may be a bit different during animations.effects and glitches. If the BL slider is grayed out it means it has no effect on that bone.

Adjusting any bone also affects all of its children. To get a sense of what adjusting one bone will do, just look at its children.
# cf_j_neck affects both neck and head since cf_j_head is parented to it, while cf_s_neck only affects the neck itself.
# cf_d_bust01_L affects entire left breast, cf_s_bust01_L only affects root part of it.

Dont be too afraid to move and rotate bones around, sometimes this is the only way to make things look good (broad shoulders for example)
If adjusting cf_d_* / j_s_* / cf_s_* bones seem to do the same thing, use cf_s_* - they are least likely to cause issues.

Things to keep in mind:
- Uneven XYZ scaling of bones with animated child bones (whole arm/leg, torso, cf_j_neck, finger roots) will produce deformities during animations.
- Rotating cf_j_* bones of the body is a bad idea - those are joits used in animation (face bones are usually fine). They may still prove useful in Studio for tweaking static poses.
- To fix face Scale sliders are generally safe to use with no major glitches. Length, offset and rotation sliders can cause glitches and misplaced body parts if used on some bones.
- glithces just reload the character. Body shape glithes (breasts drifting out of place, scewed pelvis etc.) can often only be fixed by restarting character maker.
replacement:
在角色编辑器各页用黄色 ABMX 滑块调整的骨骼会自动加入此窗口。

将鼠标移到下方列表的骨骼上可查看备注，只有部分骨骼有备注。标记为“ANIMCOR”的骨骼用于动画修正系统，调整它们可能在游戏中产生异常。
BL = Bone length，即骨长，表示当前骨骼与父骨骼的距离。有些骨骼效果明显，例如 cf_j_spine02/03，有些则不明显。也可使用偏移和旋转控制，但动画中的效果可能略有不同。BL 滑块灰显表示它对此骨骼无效。

调整一根骨骼也会影响所有子骨骼。观察子骨骼可帮助理解调整效果。
# cf_j_neck 同时影响颈部和头部，因为 cf_j_head 是它的子级，而 cf_s_neck 只影响颈部本身。
# cf_d_bust01_L 影响整个左胸，cf_s_bust01_L 只影响胸部根部。

可以尝试移动和旋转骨骼，有时这是改善外观的必要方式，例如调整宽肩。
如果调整 cf_d_* / j_s_* / cf_s_* 看起来效果相同，优先使用 cf_s_*，它们较少产生问题。

需注意：
- 对具有动画子骨骼的骨骼进行不均匀 XYZ 缩放，例如整条手臂／腿、躯干、cf_j_neck、手指根部，会在动画中产生变形。
- 旋转身体的 cf_j_* 骨骼通常不合适，因为它们是动画关节，面部骨骼一般可用。在工作室中微调静态姿势时仍可能有用。
- 调整面部时，Scale 滑块通常较安全。某些骨骼的长度、偏移和旋转滑块可能造成异常或部位错位。
- 出现异常可重新加载角色。身体形状异常，例如胸部漂移或骨盆倾斜，通常需要重启角色编辑器。

source: Welcome to Timeline, a plugin used to make advanced custom animations, here are some things you might want to know: - Close this help by pressing Help again. - Play, pause, and stop your animation with the buttons on the left of the main window. You can also use the shortcut alt + t to play/pause. - The playback time is represented by a red bar travelling through the window (called the cursor). - You can move the cursor to a specific time by clicking on the black bar above the grid. - You can also move the cursor to a specific time by changing the time text manually while paused. - You can also move the cursor by using the previous/next "frame" buttons (below play/pause/stop). Use the input field between them to set the "framerate". For example, with a value of 60, pressing the next button will move the cursor 1/60th of a second forward. - You can zoom in and out by holding left control and scrolling on the grid or just scrolling on the top black bar. - You can scroll horizontally on the grid by holding left shift and scrolling normally. - On the left of the window, you can see a list of Interpolables. In this context, an interpolable represents a variable that can be changed (interpolated between multiple values) over time. - Values are represented by red diamonds and are called Keyframes, do a middle click on the grid to add one. Protip; use left shift to snap a new keyframe to the grid. It can be used to snap things in other contexts too, try it! - Each interpolable has a set of keyframes, left click on one to open the Keyframe window: - Here you can see the time of the keyframe, its value, and a curve that represents how the value will be interpolated between this keyframe and the next. - The keyframe's timing can be modified by typing something in the input field or by clicking on Use Current Time, this has the effect to take the current playback time (where the cursor is) and set it to the keyframe. Drag At Current Time is almost the same except when multiple keyframes are selected. In this scenario, Use Current Time will try to set the same time for all the selected keyframes (if possible) while Drag At Current Time will keep the shape of the selection intact (that's why it's called Drag). More information later on what dragging in this context means. - The value can be changed by clicking on Use Current Value, this has the effect to take the current value of what you're changing (the position of an object for example) and set it to the keyframe. - The curve can be changed in multiple ways: - Add a point by doing a middle click somewhere. - You can drag and drop this point around to change its time and value. - You can use the scrollwheel on the point to change the orientation of both tangents. - For more precise changes, use the fields on the right. - To remove a point, hold left control and middle click on the point. - You can copy/paste curves between keyframes by using the two Copy/Paste buttons. - You can invert a curve by using the Invert button. - A few commonly used templates are available below those buttons, feel free to use them. - Those parameters are saved automatically, so be careful when you're changing something. - It's possible to select and edit multiple keyframes at the same time (however, some operations are limited, try it yourself and you'll see). Multi selection is done by holding left control or left shift or by simply using the selection box like you would select files in the explorer. - You can copy/cut/paste keyframes by selecting one or more, using the traditional shortcuts control + c or control + x, changing the position of the cursor, and using control + v. When doing this, the leftmost keyframe will be copied on the cursor, and the other keyframes will be copied after that. - Holding the alt key while pasting keyframes will insert them. This is a special kind of pasting operation that makes all the keyframes on the right of the cursor move so that what you're pasting has enough space to be there. - Keyframes can be dragged around by holding alt and using your mouse. Obviously you should be careful with this feature since it will change the time of the selected keyframe(s). - Selected keyframes can be scaled (i.e. you can make them closer or further apart) with alt + scroll - You can move the cursor to a specific keyframe by right clicking on it. - Keyframes can also be deleted by using control + middle click on them. Adding shift to the mix will delete all the selected keyframes plus the one clicked on. - Similar to paste insert described above, it's also possible to void delete keyframes. By holding the alt key while deleting keyframes, the ones on the right of the cursor will move back so it fills up the blank space that was left. This operation also work with control + x. - Interpolables can also be deleted by using control + middle click on them. - The list of available interpolables is linked to the object you have selected in your Workspace, so make sure to try and select everything. - Some interpolables are also linked to the selected GuideObject (that handle that allows you to move/rotate/scale an object or part of it). Which means that you can (for example) activate IK on a character and manipulate each node independently (each node will have a set of keyframes). - If you're feeling hardcore, you can enable the "All" checkbox at the top of the interpolables list, it will display interpolables across all items in your scene. - A lot of operations can be performed on interpolables via a special context menu. Try using right click on one: - Select linked GuideObject (single interpolable only): if you're confused and want to know the GuideObject linked to a certain interpolable, use this option and it will select the GuideObject (if applicable) or the character/item in the workspace. The same thing can be achieved by holding alt while clicking on the interpolable. The opposite can also be done when holding alt and selecting a GuideObject. This will highlight for a few seconds the linked interpolable (if any). - Rename (single interpolable only): allows you to change the name of an interpolable. If you already have a custom name set, emptying the text field will make the interpolable return to its original name. - Group together (multiple interpolables only): while having multiple interpolable selected (with either control + click or shift + click), you can group them together. This action will create a dedicated line that represents the group that can be collapsed or expanded (like a folder). More on that later. - Select keyframes: selects all the keyframes of the selected interpolable(s). - Select keyframes before cursor: selects all the keyframes of the selected interpolables(s) (only those before the cursor). - Select keyframes after cursor: selects all the keyframes of the selected interpolables(s) (only those after the cursor). - Color : this allows you to change the background color of the interpolable, very useful for organisation. - Add keyframe(s) at cursor: for each interpolable selected, this option adds one or several new keyframe(s) where the cursor is. A similar action can also be achieved through the shortcut alt + middle click on the grid. However, this one will add the keyframes where the mouse is, and not where the cursor is. This can also be combined with other shortcuts like shift. - Parent to: used to parent interpolables to a certain group, or unparent them altogether. - Disable (all)/Enable (all): used to disable/enable all the selected interpolables. - Move up/down: moves interpolables up or down in the list, also very useful for organisation. - Delete: removes interpolables and their keyframes. - Groups also have a dedicated context menu: - Rename: rename the group. - Select Interpolables under: select all the interpolables under this group. - Select keyframes: select all the keyframes of all the interpolables under this group. - Select keyframes before cursor: select all the keyframes of all the interpolables under this group (only those before the cursor). - Select keyframes after cursor: select all the keyframes of all the interpolables under this group (only those after the cursor). - Add keyframes at cursor: same as above but for all the interpolables under this group. - Parent to: parent the whole group to another group, or unparent it altogether. - Disable/Enable: used disable/enable all the interpolables under this group. - Move up/down: same as the one for interpolables. - Delete: removes the whole group and all the interpolables within!. - Finally, groups can be collapsed/expanded via a single left click on them. - Interpolables on an object can be saved through the Single Files menu. If a character is selected, its active animation will also be saved in the same file. - Filter interpolables by their name with the text field below the list. - Different "time signatures" can be used if you change the Block Length and Divisions fields. Block Length determines the length in seconds of a block, and Divisions is the number of smaller parts in a block. This can be useful if you want your grid to sync up with a specific tempo, for example. - The whole UI can become semi transparent by holding control and using the scrollwheel on the word "Timeline" on the interface. That's it!
